summary: gcp-log-poc exfiltrates full environment to attacker-controlled GCP project at install and import time
details: The package runs identical exfiltration code from both setup.py (executed on sdist install) and gcp_log_poc/__init__.py (executed on every `import gcp_log_poc`). On each trigger it collects host identifiers, the installer's public IP (fetched from api.ipify.org), and the entire `os.environ` dict, then ships the payload to Google Cloud Logging under the project `nginxinc` using `log_struct`. Authentication to that logging sink uses a GCP service-account JSON embedded in the source as a large base64 blob that is XOR-decoded at runtime with the hardcoded key `poc-dep-confusion-2026`; the decoded JSON is loaded via `service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_info` and passed to `google.cloud.logging.Client(project="nginxinc")`. The `nginxinc` project name and the XOR-key string identify this as a dependency-confusion payload targeting the nginxinc namespace. Environment variables routinely contain CI secrets, cloud credentials, and registry tokens, so a bulk `os.environ` dump to a destination the installer did not configure is credential exfiltration against the installing host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
